reviews.title: Legit works for diastasis recti
reviews.contents:
I had not worked out since my 3rd C-section, 7 years ago, because my diastasis recti was so bad and I felt so discouraged and it was so uncomfortable.  When I tried to do a crunch, it looked like an alien was trying to jump out of me.  Random strangers would ask me when I was due.  My OB, during my annual exam, said to me “your abdominal area has just completely given up, hasn’t it.”  When I started with this app and did the first gap measurement, it felt like I could get both hand’s worth of fingers (so 8 fingers) into the gap, it was ridiculous.  This app was a Hail Mary before I started looking for surgeons (that I can’t really afford).

I have now been doing the exercises in this app at least 5 days a week for 6 weeks.  Dear lord is it effective.  I’m down to a two finger gap, and just a tiny little “gently sloping hill” when I try to do a crunch.  I’ve lost .7 inch in my waist and .4 inch in my stomach.  And the very best part is I can do the whole thing in my room with the door closed right after taking the kids to school before I head to the office.  One time I couldn’t get the exercises in, and I literally did at least the core compressions in the car while driving to work. It’s easy and it feels good to do them.

The only negative to this app is that my husband is a little miffed that I started spending so much money on new tops that are small and cute, instead of the tents I was wearing to hide my belly.  Good problems.  :)

reviews.title: Getting good results
reviews.contents: I’m 21 days in and I really like this app. I had a diastases after my first pregnancy and didn’t really know what to do about it. I’d always been very active, but was afraid to take on any abdominal exercises in fear of making things worse. After my second baby, I knew I had to seek out professional help. I started going to a class run by a Physical Therapist who specializes in pelvic floor/core/women’s health when my baby was around 3 months old. I also met with her for a few one on one sessions. When my baby was about 7 months old, I downloaded the Every Mother app. The app has really helped me to be consistent with my exercises and get stronger. In just 3 weeks, I’ve seen a big difference in the strength of my core and it also looks tighter, as well. I’ve been more consistent with the app exercises, than with the exercises that the PT gave me. I like that I can follow along with a video for every workout. I love that the app mixes the exercises up - this keeps things from getting boring. I also love the layout of if the app. It’s very easy to use. And most important of all, it keeps me engaged, on track and motivated. I love that each exercise/day get checked off - this is as satisfying as crossing something off of your to do this. I like that there is a visible record   of all you have accomplished and all that still needs to be completed. I would love it if you could input some information to personalize the app - add the date that you start and you initial measurements. Great app! Nice work!

reviews.title: Love it!! Very Helpful information and professionals
reviews.contents: This app is a great gentle workout. I love that it is safe for DR and also helps to heal it! I’m still on week 3 so I’m not very far in, but I love the workouts and gentleness of the trainer and also the helpful videos which tell you what is safe and what is not and how to properly move day to day with DR. I cried when I watched those because I felt so supported and like I was finally getting the information I needed! I love that you can ask questions and a trained professional will answer you. I’m feeling like I can do it! It’s so nice that the videos are easy to follow, especially with motherhood really taking it all out of me everyday, I love that I can come to this app and do similar workouts everyday, not having to learn something new necessarily. I feel like the moves are specifically chosen for their effectiveness because I can feel it. I really like the speakers voice and her words are always helpful reminders so I’m properly doing the exercises! I often find myself listening to her and then realizing I needed that reminder and incorporating it. I also really love the set up of the app, it’s straightforward but also simple and beautiful. Thanks EveryMother

reviews.title: Not doctor recommended
reviews.contents: I’m currently disappointed in this program. I wasn’t able to see what the exercises would be before paying $60 and creating an account, and then once I was able to see the exercises and attempt to do them, I discovered that some of them are not recommended by my doctor and others are actually impossible/dangerous when you’re six months pregnant with twins. For example, my doctor told me to not do side planks (part of the first day of exercises), because that could create further abdominal separation, as I have two babies pulling their weight down on that side. She also said the breathing exercises aren’t necessarily bad, but I should try to breathe normally at all times, as it can be hard enough to do that without changing your breathing pattern. The second day of exercise featured a yoga flow that told me to bend in half at the waist. That’s just…not possible right now, and it would put strain on my back. There was no modification given. It’s also distressing that the people demonstrating the exercises aren’t pregnant. Sure, it’s super easy for them to just bend every which way, but it doesn’t make me feel like these programs are tailored for pregnancy. All in all, I’m just very disappointed that there’s no sort of money back or trial with this program, as it has been deemed not safe for me and also pretty misleading. Maybe it’s great postpartum, but it isn’t safe or even that feasible during pregnancy, and there’s no way to recoup your $60 after you find that out.

reviews.title: Three years of charges for an app I didn't even have installed
reviews.contents:
I signed up for Every Mother in 2023 during my first pregnancy, used it for about a month, and believed I had cancelled. I hadn't had the app downloaded on any device since — no logins, no usage, nothing — yet I was charged for a full annual membership renewal in 2024, 2025, and again attempted in 2026.
I only discovered this because a payment method I'd since cancelled for unrelated reasons triggered a "please update your card" email. Otherwise, this likely would have continued indefinitely.
When I reached out, their support (a mix of an AI bot and then a human rep) confirmed the account would be cancelled going forward, but declined to refund any of the past charges, citing a blanket no-refund policy. I understand every company needs a policy, but three years of charges for a completely inactive account is a different situation than someone simply changing their mind — and I was disappointed that no exception was possible even after a "human review."
I came to this company during one of the most exhausted, overextended seasons of my life — pregnant or postpartum for three years straight — and I think that's exactly the kind of situation a company built around supporting mothers should be able to show some flexibility for. I'd encourage anyone signing up to set a calendar reminder to double check your cancellation went through, because their system will keep billing you indefinitely without any usage-based checks or reminders

reviews.title: Slimming my waist
reviews.contents: I’ve tried quite a few diastasis programs in the past but this one is the best. The easy to use app format is my favorite vs trying to find what day I’m on with programs available online. I just switched from a different workout app (which wasn’t geared for DR) because it was destroying my core despite trying to be careful. I had undone all of my previous DR healing unfortunately by doing certain excersises I didn’t realize were harmful, and by not engaging my core properly. My pooch became huge after faithfully following that workout program for 74 days and I felt so defeated! I had been eyeing every mother program and decided it was time to switch. I’m only a little over one week in and my DR is closing back up thankfully and my pooch is almost completely gone. I will add though, I already know how to activate my deep transverse muscles. You need to be careful about your posture and proper core engagement throughout the day as well for EM to be as effective as quickly as it has been for me. I’m hoping to completely close my DR by the end of the program!

reviews.title: Does not support sensory disabilities
reviews.contents:
If you can see and hear perfectly you will have no difficulty. I am partially deaf so I have to have to volume very loud, which means my baby has to be awake when I do it, which makes it hard to do. Supposedly a selection of videos have cc, but I’m 32 days in and have yet to encounter any. 
And no, there is no descriptive audio offered for the blind, otherwise my blind friend could have signed for me as I went through the motions. That was a very frustrating afternoon for both of us.
Do the workouts actually work? The core compression stretches seem to have had an impact, and they are safer for postpartum recovery than Fitbit’s offerings. However they are a bit repetitive in sequence and there’s almost no modifications offered if you have injuries/disabilities. (The repetitive nature isn’t all bad, I’m deaf not stupid and it did allow me to memorize the moves so I could work out quietly) 
Also keep in mind the actual workouts increase in length so if you are looking for 10-15th every day instead of 30 you’ll need to check their library for alternatives. 
Overall, I’d recommend over Fitbits workouts, but would really like to see updates that make it easier for the audio and visually impaired.

reviews.title: Agenda Driven Company
reviews.contents: I was really interested in this app which was brought to my attention through an ad in my Instagram feed. I currently have diastis recti and was excited at the idea of using an app and at-home program to help get it under control versus going to a physical therapist weekly as i have been doing. Unfortunately, I went on Instagram to check out the vibe of Every Mother‘s social media and was disappointed to find posts dedicated to the LGTBQ+ lifestyle, the Black Lives Matter Marxist movement, race education for youth, and other virtue signaling messages. The posts mentioned are all fine and good except for the fact that there wasn’t a single patriotic post dedicated to our beautiful country on any of the days the opportunity for such a post would have been ideal such as memorial day, the Fourth of July, or Veterans Day. The Every Mother team claims to support mothers and families in the armed services, but how exactly? I see no posts, where the app is most publicly represented, dedicated to support of those mothers/families or our country. The founders of Every Mother may have selfishly forgotten about what many have sacrificed to allow them to even have an app to begin with, but I will forgo purchasing or supporting them while I wear red, white, and blue for all the black, white, and brown brothers and sisters who served and died to make this the best country in the world. 🇺🇸

reviews.title: It really works
reviews.contents: I was going to wait til I finished the reclaim program (90 days) but after the check in at day 42 I can say with absolute certainty this program WORKS. I knew I was feeling different but wasn’t positive I looked any different. My weight is the same (I’m not overweight but have a belly) but after taking the check in photos I was like WOW there has been significant change! The first couple weeks I didn’t have tons of motivation but I did have disciple and once I had completed 21 days it’s become a habit. I feel incomplete if I don’t do the workout for the day and now seeing the progress I feel a huge motivation boost to keep going. This is the key: stick with it, be consistent for at least 21 days and just see for yourself. I do the core compressions and also the workouts. It feels too easy a lot of days but some days it can really push me. Either way it’s definitely working so I’m likely going to get the year subscription once I finish reclaim. I’m honestly just shocked how effective it is because it’s so doable!

reviews.title: Like it but could do with some tweaks
reviews.contents: Generally happy with both the app and the training videos, but there a few things that I haven’t liked. Several of the exercise videos require equipment like weights, resistance bands, blocks, etc., I wish it was more clear from the onset what equipment will be needed with details (like actual weigh ranges rather than “light” and “heavy”). Some videos are of an instructor doing the moves and voice-over directions. I find these difficult to keep up with and have even injured my back slightly trying to both do the move and watch the video to figure out what to do simultaneously. Videos where the instructor is talking and doing the moves live are much easier to keep up with. My guided path is 84 days long and my subscription is 91 days, which doesn’t give me much time for days off unless I pay for another 3-month subscription. Otherwise, I like the mix of weight training, cardio, and yoga and I can say after 3 weeks I already notice improvements to my body. I’ll likely continue using this app after my initial path ends.
